description:
FILED s473w (Opus, 2026-09-09) while probing #1507 (`use overload` is a BEGIN).
PRE-EXISTING: identical on `0ece3088` and on the #1507 tree, so #1507 did not
cause it and does not fix it.

`no overload 'OP'` is IGNORED.  perl's `overload::unimport` REMOVES the named
handler, after which the operator falls back (with `fallback => 1`) to the
remaining ones.  PCL keeps the handler.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3):

    { package F;
      use overload '""' => sub { "F<".${$_[0]}.">" }, '0+' => sub { 42 },
                   fallback => 1;
      no overload '0+';
      sub new { my ($c,$v)=@_; bless \$v, $c } }
    my $f = F->new(3);
    print "$f", " ", ($f+0), "\n";

    perl:  F<3> 0     # the 0+ handler is gone; fallback numifies "F<3>" -> 0
    PCL:   F<3> 42    # the 0+ handler is still installed

WHERE: `Pl/Parser.pm::_process_use_overload` handles the `use` side only; the
`no` side reaches the generic pragma path and emits nothing.  The runtime has
`p-register-overloads` and no un-register.  The fix is one runtime entry point
(remove the named keys from the package's table) plus the `no overload` arm in
the same v1 routine â and it must land in the same COMPILE-phase bucket #1507
put the `use` side in, since perl's `no` is a BEGIN too and their relative
source order is what decides the result.

SIZE: small, but no board or sweep row is known to sit behind it â found by a
probe, filed on its own merits.  Related but different: DECIDED s464 records
that `nomethod` is ignored and the BITWISE ops have no overload dispatch
(#972); this is a third hole in the same model.
subject: `no overload OP` is ignored â the handler stays installed where perl removes it and falls back (probed; a third hole beside #972 nomethod and the bitwise ops)
